newsitem.title: PANAMA: Central America unity strong even without Panama.
newsitem.headline: Central America unity strong even without Panama.

text.p: Panama's decision to skip a Central American summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton next month will not endanger the region's relations with Washington, Guatemalan Foreign Minister Eduardo Stein said on Thursday.
"We don't think the absence of Panama will signify any break with relations in the region with Washington," he told reporters at a one-day regional meeting of foreign ministers.
At a regional presidential summit with Clinton on May 8 in San Jose, Costa Rica, Central American leaders plan to propose a free trade agreement with the United States.

"We believe it (the summit) is an opportunity to re-launch regional relations with the United States, but we recognise the particular agenda Panama has with the United States and, of course, we would never want to interfere," Stein said.

Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares explained this week his decision not to attend the San Jose meeting by saying, "the Central Americans are interested in topics that for us don't have any significance, and vice versa."
"We are interested in bilateral relations with the United States, the (Panama Canal) treaties and the creation of a multinational drug interdiction center" in Panama, he added.
